subject: Scout debrief: verified TPS/latency pack + pilot ops checklist
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@cleardata.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scout debrief: verified TPS/latency pack + pilot ops checklist

Hi Ava — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our scout/discovery call and the immediate things we can share to help you qualify Redwood for the search+ranking pilot. I captured model-fit suggestions plus verified performance snapshots attached. TL;DR: we recommend running a small pilot on the 13B quantized variant first, then scale to the 70B only if quality gaps persist.

Recap (short):
- Goal you shared: relevance ranking across 10M doc corpus, sub-100ms p95 latency for interactive UX, and 1500 TPS peak for background re-ranks.
- Constraints: VPC-only logs, SOC2 evidence for audit, and procurement timeline in Q4.

Redwood-verified model shortlist (recommendation order):
1) Llama-2-13B-q4_0 (recommended start) — stable verifications on commodity A100-equivalent nodes, best cost/latency balance.
2) RedWood-13B-FT (task-finetuned candidate) — higher relevance for <2x cost; keep for canary.
3) Llama-2-70B-8bit (fallback for edge quality cases) — higher p99 and cost.

Benchmarks attached / links:
- Verified TPS profiles: p50/p95/p99 latency snapshots per model and sequence length included (latency-snapshots.csv).
- End-to-end traces and example prompts: cleardata-eval-traces.zip (sample payloads, KV cache profiles).
- Prompt set we used for your domain (sample queries) in prompt-pack-v2.md.

Quick performance summary (from our Redwood verification harness):
- Llama-2-13B-q4_0 @ batch=8: steady-state 1,800 TPS (small tokens), p50=14ms, p95=48ms, p99=82ms on a single A100-40GB equivalent instance (continuous batching enabled).
- RedWood-13B-FT @ batch=6: 1,100 TPS, p50=21ms, p95=72ms, p99=120ms (higher quality in our ranking evals).
- Llama-2-70B-8bit @ batch=4: 420 TPS, p50=60ms, p95=210ms, p99=420ms.

Notes on quality/regression guardrails: we saw a small regression in named-entity recall for generative reranks on older prompt versions; updated prompt-pack-v2.md reduces hallucination by anchoring scoring to document spans. We also recommend adding the regression guard set from the Drive link to CI to catch quality drift during quantization changes.

Immediate next steps we propose:
- SE technical pilot: 60–90 minute throughput validation (we’ll run your small sample and share run traces) — owner: Dev Patel.
- Procurement checklist & SOC2 pack: Marcus to share the compliance bundle and T&Cs.
- Pilot schedule: proposed week of Oct 18 for pilot run.

Attachments: cleardata-eval-traces.zip (archive), latency-snapshots.csv (CSV), prompt-pack-v2.md (text).

Can you confirm which env (VPC region / account) you'd like us to use for the pilot and whether procurement wants a formal SOW? Happy to sync and set calendar.

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Scout debrief: verified TPS/latency pack + pilot ops checklist

Hi Ava — jumping in with the infra details and a quick ops checklist for the SE validation run.

Infra used for the 13B steady-state numbers:
- Node spec used: A100-equivalent (NVIDIA A100 40GB) - 1 GPU for the single-node traces we shared; continuous batching and KV cache reduced per-token work.
- For your 1,500 TPS target we recommend a small pool of 2 nodes (autoscale to 3 for headroom) in Dedicated or Private depending on VPC requirements. That gives ~3,200 TPS steady-state with similar p95 headroom.

Cost estimate (pilot window, rough):
- 2-week validation (2x A100 nodes, 24/7): ~$12K (compute) + Redwood pilot support (SRE/SE hours) ~$4K.
- 2-week observation + light load: ~$3K.
- Total ballpark pilot: ~$19K (we'll produce a formal SOW for procurement).

Additional perf detail (sample, internal-verif harness v3):
- Llama-2-13B-q4_0: sequence=64 tokens, batch=8 -> median latency 14ms, p95 48ms, p99 82ms; tail variance correlated to cold-cache microbursts (we see ~1.5–2x p99 when cache miss + long sequence).
- Recommendations to reduce tail: enable prefix caching for repeated queries, set token limit at generation step where possible, and use dynamic batching thresholds in the Redwood runtime.

Prompt sets & CI: attached prompt-pack-v2.md contains the curated prompts we ran; please include your high-value queries so we can add them to the regression guard set.

SE-run checklist (short):
1) Provide sample corpus (<= 10k items) and representative traffic profile (we can accept anonymized payloads).
2) Provide VPC region and a list of IP allowlists.
3) Approve running a 90-minute throughput run (we'll produce perf traces + contention analysis).
4) Confirm procurement path for pilot (SOW or PO).

I'll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff with your infra/ML engineer if that helps — suggested slot: Oct 12 or Oct 13.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Attachment references: prompt-pack-v2.md, cleardata-eval-traces.zip, latency-snapshots.csv
